title: Margaret River
description: A maritime corner of Western Australia making elegant, Bordeaux-like Cabernet and world-class Chardonnay.
L: Margaret River lies in the far south-west of Western Australia, about 270 km south of Perth, on a peninsula between the Indian Ocean to the west and the Southern Ocean to the south. It's about 110 km long and narrow. It has about 5,500 hectares of vines, only around 3% of Australia's, but around 20% of its premium wine.

Margaret River has a maritime, Mediterranean climate, among the most maritime in Australia. Oceans moderate temperatures: small differences between summer and winter, and between day and night. Most rain falls in winter. Summers are warm, not hot. Soils are gravelly, sandy loams over granite, draining well. Strong winds in spring can affect flowering.

In 1965, Dr John Gladstones, an agricultural scientist, published research suggesting the region's climate was similar to Bordeaux's. Doctors founded the first wineries: Vasse Felix in 1967, then Moss Wood and Cullen. Leeuwin Estate, from the 1970s, made world-class Chardonnay. In a few decades it became one of Australia's top regions.

Margaret River Cabernet Sauvignon, often blended with Merlot, is elegant and structured, with blackcurrant, cedar, herbs and fine tannins. It's frequently compared with Bordeaux. Producers like Cullen, Moss Wood, Vasse Felix and Cape Mentelle are famous. Cabernet is the region's most important red.

Margaret River Chardonnay is among Australia's best: rich yet fresh, with stone fruit, citrus, nuts and oak. Leeuwin Estate's Art Series Chardonnay is iconic. Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc blends, called SBS or SSB, are a local speciality: crisp, herbal, citrus and fresh, inspired by Bordeaux whites.

Labels show the grape or blend, Margaret River GI, and vintage, with Australia's 85% rules. Blends list grapes by share, like Cabernet Merlot. SBS or SSB indicates which white grape dominates. Screw caps are standard. Some producers name single vineyards or sub-regions, like Wilyabrup, an informal area home to several founding estates.

Margaret River Cabernet suits lamb, beef and kangaroo; Chardonnay suits marron, a local freshwater crayfish, lobster and roast chicken; SBS suits oysters, fish and salads. The region is also known for surf, forests and seafood. Serve Cabernet at 16 to 18 degrees, Chardonnay at 10 to 12, SBS at 7 to 9.
